result.title: Spectral symmetry fingerprints in equivariant representations
result.summary: Symmetry governs the organization of physical structures, while symmetry breaking reveals their transformations. In geometric deep learning, symmetry imposes rank constraints on equivariant representations, limiting the expressive capacity of equivariant graph neural networks (GNNs). Here we show that these constraints can instead be exploited: the singular-value spectra of equivariant representations provide a unified fingerprint of structural symmetry. We introduce spectral symmetry fingerprints (SymFP), which enable discrete point-group identification through rank-template matching and continuous symmetry analysis by quantifying spectral energy beyond target rank constraints. SymFP is orientation invariant and architecture agnostic, enabling a parameter-free GNN implementation. Its spectra can be reused across multiple target groups, and the resulting leakage scores satisfy subgroup monotonicity. Across synthetic structures, molecules, coordination complexes and large biological assemblies, SymFP accurately identifies point groups, tracks controlled symmetry breaking and reveals local and degree-resolved symmetry changes that can be obscured by global geometric measures. These results establish the spectral structure of equivariant representations as a general framework for characterizing symmetry across physical systems.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 SymFP，用等变表示的奇异值谱作为结构对称性的统一指纹：通过秩模板匹配识别离散点群，并以超出目标秩约束的谱能量量化连续对称破缺，在合成结构、分子、配合物与大型生物组装上验证其识别与追踪局部、按度数分辨的对称变化的能力。
AI.relevance_reason: 与 LVR 主线无直接关联，但其「用内部表示的奇异值谱刻画被保留与被约束的信息」这一诊断思路，可能启发对 latent 视觉状态中几何与任务必要信息保留程度、以及表示秩约束如何限制推理容量的核查。
